rv.q: This might be a work of outlandish genius, or a devised end of year A-level project featuring world-class actors (led by Ralph Fiennes and Francesca Annis).
As a closing note for Fiennes ’ season, Small Hotel is a quiet, thoughtful choice, one that leans into the experimental rather than the crowd-pleasing.
Ralph Fiennes stars in Rebecca Lenkiewicz’s opaque new play
As the last of three productions presented under Ralph Fiennes’ stewardship in Bath, Small Hotel offers some of the best work of the season.
You’re likely to leave feeling decidedly unrewarded by the play, which not only offers us themes of resentment and regret, but is a missed opportunity in itself.
Small Hotel is a triumph not because it provides easy answers, but because it doesn't try to.

cn.t: Fiennes' season closer divides critics with its elliptical, dreamlike structure and surprising tap-dancing flourishes. Some find Lenkiewicz's meditation on love and regret quietly devastating; others deem it bizarre and baffling.
